QF.id: SIA Social Stock Exchange Introduction and Instruments_15

question.text: A social enterprise must be engaged in one of the eligible activities specified under which regulation of the SEBI ICDR Regulations, 2018, to raise funds on the SSE?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 2.3.1.3, ZCZPs 'shall be issued only for a specific project or activity that are listed under regulation 292E of the SEBI (ICDR) Regulations'. Regulation 292E enumerates the 16 eligible activities (hunger/poverty eradication, healthcare, education, gender equality, environmental sustainability, heritage protection, rural sports, incubator support, etc.). Regulation 292I governs the instrument itself; 292J covers ZCZP eligibility; 292B is the general ICDR Chapter X-A definitions. The Trap: Option A (292B) covers definitions of terms. Option C (292I) covers ZCZP issuance rules. Option D (292J) covers ZCZP eligibility criteria for the issuer — a related but distinct regulation. Cross-Exam Context: III-A / III-C (Compliance) track Chapter X-A references. XIX-A/B/C/D/E treat AIF Regulation 10 investable-funds mirrors. Assessor's Pro-Tip: In your engagement letter, cite the specific Regulation 292E sub-clause (i through xvi) matching the NPO's activity bucket — naming the exact sub-clause sharpens the scope statement and avoids 'activity drift' during fieldwork.
